topics.title: Using AI assistants well at work
topics.what: Getting reliable, high-quality help from assistants like Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini: giving context, checking output, and knowing what they're bad at.
topics.why: Assistants now take on multi-step work (research, documents, files, browsing), not just chat. The gap between casual and skilled users keeps widening.

how.1: Take a free AI fluency course, then use an assistant on one real task a day.
how.2: Build reusable prompts or projects for your repeat tasks; learn when to verify and when to trust.

refs.t: Anthropic Academy: AI Fluency and Claude 101

topics.title: How LLMs actually work
topics.what: Tokens, context windows, next-token prediction, temperature, and why 'reasoning' or 'thinking' models spend extra tokens before answering.
topics.why: Every product decision (cost, speed, reliability) traces back to these basics. Models now ship with 1M-token context windows and adjustable reasoning effort, so knowing what those mean pays off.

how.1: Watch one intuitive explainer end to end.
how.2: Learn tokens, context limits and reasoning effort; test them in a playground.
how.3: Build a tiny language model or follow a from-scratch course.
how.4: Go deep on architectures, scaling and inference.

Andrej Karpathy: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
Karpathy: Neural Networks, Zero to Hero
Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch

topics.title: Prompting → context engineering
topics.what: Designing everything the model sees: instructions, examples, retrieved documents, tool results and memory, not just the wording of one prompt.
topics.why: The 2026 shift: agents run for many steps, so what goes into (and gets dropped from) their context decides quality and cost. Prompt caching price cuts make long, stable context cheaper.

how.1: Learn the basics: be specific, give examples, say the format you want.
how.2: Use structured prompts, examples and step-by-step instructions on real tasks.
how.3: Manage context for agents: compaction, retrieval, tool results, caching.
how.4: Measure context strategies with evals; design memory for long-running agents.

refs.t: Anthropic: Effective context engineering for AI agents

topics.title: Coding agents
topics.what: Tools like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor that read a codebase, edit files, run tests and fix bugs from a plain-language goal.
topics.why: At the 2026 AI Engineer World's Fair the headline was 'coding agents replace IDEs'. Knowing how to steer them (plans, tests, review) is now a core engineering skill.

how.1: Try one coding agent on a small personal project.
how.2: Use a coding agent daily; learn to give it a plan and a test to pass.
how.3: Set up project instructions, custom commands and CI checks for agents.
how.4: Run agents in parallel, automate with the SDKs, and measure their output quality.

refs.t: Latent Space: 5 trends from AI Engineer World's Fair 2026

topics.title: Agents and the harness around them
topics.what: LLMs that plan and act in a loop with tools. The 2026 focus is the 'harness': permissions, context, human checkpoints and feedback loops around the model.
topics.why: Engineers are moving from building one-off agents to 'loop engineering': agents run the inner loop, humans steer the outer loop with evals and review.

how.2: Learn the difference between workflows and agents; try an agent product.
how.3: Build a small agent with an SDK; add tools, limits and a human approval step.
how.4: Design multi-agent systems, long-running tasks and recovery from failure.

refs.t: Anthropic: Writing effective tools for agents

topics.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
topics.what: An open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data. An MCP server exposes tools, resources and prompts; any MCP-capable client (Claude, ChatGPT, IDEs, agents) can use it.
topics.why: The 2026-07-28 spec is the biggest update yet: a stateless core (no initialize handshake or session IDs, so servers scale behind load balancers), multi-round-trip requests for mid-call confirmations, header-based routing, cacheable list results, and hardened OAuth (Client ID Metadata Documents replace dynamic client registration). Sampling, Roots, Logging and the old HTTP+SSE transport are deprecated. The August roadmap adds agent identity, long-running tasks and progressive tool discovery.

how.2: Understand what MCP is and connect an existing MCP server to your assistant.
how.3: Build a small MCP server with the Python or TypeScript SDK against the 2026-07-28 spec.
how.4: Migrate servers to the stateless model and new auth; deploy behind a gateway.

refs.t: WorkOS: What changes for agent authentication

topics.title: Agent Skills
topics.what: Folders of instructions, scripts and resources that an agent loads only when a task needs them, so it can follow your team's way of doing things.
topics.why: One of the five trends of 2026: agent platforms are organising around skills because they're portable, reusable and cut orchestration code.

how.2: Install and use a ready-made skill in your assistant.
how.3: Write a skill for a workflow your team repeats.
how.4: Build a skill library with evaluation and versioning.

refs.t: Anthropic: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills

topics.title: Tool use and structured outputs
topics.what: Letting a model call functions you define and return data in an exact JSON shape your code can trust.
topics.why: Every agent and integration is built on this. Newer models make fewer tool calls for the same result (e.g. Meta reports ~20% fewer in Muse Spark 1.3), so tool design matters more than volume.

how.3: Add one tool and a structured output to an app.
how.4: Design tool sets for agents: naming, descriptions, error messages, token budgets.

refs.t: Anthropic: Writing effective tools for agents

topics.title: Retrieval (RAG) and memory
topics.what: Fetching the right documents or facts and giving them to the model at answer time, plus memory that carries across sessions.
topics.why: With 1M-token context windows common, the question is now when to retrieve versus when to just include everything, and how to keep long-running agents' memory accurate.

how.3: Build a basic RAG pipeline over your own documents.
how.4: Improve retrieval with hybrid search, reranking and contextual chunking; evaluate it.

topics.title: Evals and observability
topics.what: Measuring whether your AI feature actually works: test sets, graders (including LLM-as-judge), error analysis and production tracing.
topics.why: Evals are the 'outer loop' that lets humans steer agents. Teams that measure ship faster and catch regressions when they switch models, which now happens every few weeks.

how.2: Learn why evals matter and how to read a benchmark critically.
how.3: Write a small eval set for one feature and run it on two models.
how.4: Build continuous evals, error analysis and tracing into your release process.

refs.t: Hamel Husain: Your AI product needs evals
Claude docs: Define success criteria and build evals

topics.title: Open-weight models and running AI locally
topics.what: Models whose weights you can download and run yourself (Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Llama, Nemotron, MiMo), plus the tools to run them.
topics.why: Open models are close to the frontier: Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters), GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4 have MIT-style licences, and compression like 1.76-bit ternary weights lets 27B models run on small hardware.

how.2: Run a small model on your laptop with Ollama.
how.3: Compare an open model with an API model on your own task.
how.4: Serve open models efficiently (vLLM, quantisation) and weigh licences.

topics.title: Multimodal and voice
topics.what: Models that see images and video, listen and speak in real time, and generate images or audio.
topics.why: September 2026 brought native omnimodal models (Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash), Gemini 3.8 TTS with 150+ voices, and real-time speaking avatars. Voice agents are becoming a mainstream interface.

how.2: Try voice mode and image understanding on real tasks.
how.3: Add image input or speech to an app.
how.4: Build real-time voice agents; handle latency and turn-taking.

topics.title: Cost, speed and choosing models
topics.what: Picking the right model for each job, and cutting cost and latency with prompt caching, batching, routing and smaller models.
topics.why: Prices keep falling fast: GPT-6 Sol and Luna launched about 50% cheaper than their predecessors, Claude Opus 5.5 is 40% cheaper than Opus 5, and cache reads dropped sharply. Diffusion language models reach 1,000+ tokens per second.

how.2: Learn the price and speed tiers of the models you use.
how.3: Add prompt caching and batching; route easy tasks to small models.
how.4: Build cost and latency dashboards; evaluate model swaps automatically.

refs.t: Artificial Analysis: model speed and price comparisons

topics.title: Fine-tuning and post-training
topics.what: Adapting models with your own data: supervised fine-tuning, preference tuning and reinforcement learning.
topics.why: Labs are gaining most of their improvements from post-training and RL (e.g. Grok 4.7's extended RL, Kimi-based models trained for shorter reasoning). Small teams can now fine-tune open models cheaply.

how.3: Understand when fine-tuning beats prompting (usually it doesn't).
how.4: Fine-tune an open model with LoRA; learn RLHF and RL from verifiable rewards.

topics.title: AI security, safety and trust
topics.what: Prompt injection, data leaks through tools, agent permissions and identity, and the safety practices labs and regulators expect.
topics.why: Agents act on real systems, so a malicious web page or document can steer them. The MCP 2026 spec hardens OAuth and the roadmap adds agent identity; labs now gate some cyber-capable models.

how.1: Learn the main risks of sharing data with AI tools.
how.2: Understand prompt injection and least-privilege for AI tools.
how.3: Threat-model your AI feature against the OWASP LLM Top 10.
how.4: Design agent permissions, sandboxing and auth; red-team your agents.

topics.title: Designing AI products
topics.what: UX patterns for AI: setting expectations, showing uncertainty, handling errors, human control and trust.
topics.why: Interfaces are shifting from chat boxes to agents that act and ask clarifying questions (Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 does this by design). Good AI UX is now a differentiator.

how.1: Learn the basic patterns for AI features.
how.2: Study how leading AI products handle errors and trust.
how.3: Prototype an AI feature with real model output, not placeholders.
how.4: Design agent experiences: approvals, progress, undo, handoff.

refs.t: Microsoft HAX guidelines for human-AI interaction

topics.title: AI strategy, ROI and regulation
topics.what: Where AI creates value in a business, how to measure it, how to roll it out safely, and what regulations require.
topics.why: AI is entering enterprises through 'forward deployed engineers' and platform teams. Leaders need to pick use cases, budget for fast-falling prices, and track rules like the EU AI Act.

how.1: Take a non-technical AI overview course.
how.2: Map three use cases in your team with clear success measures.
how.3: Build an adoption plan with evals, security review and cost tracking.
how.4: Set AI governance: model choice, vendor risk, compliance.
